lp.hero.title: The clipboard doesn't tell you the dose is late.
lp.hero.sub: PlantãoVet turns every prescription into tasks with a time on them, surfaces whatever ran past its window on its own, and hands the next shift a patient list that already knows where the last one stopped.
lp.hero.note: 14 days free. No card. Your clinic is live in two minutes.
lp.sheet.aria: Inpatient sheet showing the 10pm dose crossing its tolerance window
lp.sheet.footLate: The 10pm dipyrone crossed its window. Nobody had to go looking.
lp.scene.c: On the clipboard, it's still the same line it always was.
lp.scene.turn: In PlantãoVet, it already changed colour.
lp.flow.title: One line of a prescription becomes a schedule that chases itself.
lp.flow.sub: The vet prescribes once. The system works out the times from your clinic's anchor hours, and every time becomes a task with an owner, a state and a record.
lp.flow.a.title: What was prescribed
lp.flow.a.body: Drug, dose, route and frequency. What the vet would write on the sheet.
lp.flow.b.title: When it actually happens
lp.flow.b.body: q8h against your anchors becomes 10am, 6pm and 2am. Configurable, your ICU's night is yours.
lp.flow.c.title: What actually happened
lp.flow.c.body: Each time keeps who did it and when. Anything past its window turns red.
lp.late.title: Late work comes to you, not the other way round.
lp.late.sub: Every task carries a tolerance window that depends on how critical it is. Past the window, it rises to the board and to the shift console. Nobody has to remember to check the clipboard hourly.
lp.late.note: These are the starting values, based on ISMP ranges. Each clinic tunes its own: an ICU on infusion pumps and a quiet post-op ward don't share a definition of late.
lp.handover.title: The information doesn't leave with the person going home.
lp.handover.sub: At the end of the shift the report is already built, counted from the database, not from anyone's memory. Whoever takes over accepts patient by patient, with the open items in view at the moment of acceptance.
lp.handover.item.done: What was done, and by whom
lp.handover.item.notDone: What wasn't done, with the reason recorded
lp.handover.item.pending: What's still open, and what's already late
lp.handover.item.changes: Prescriptions that changed during the shift
lp.handover.line: The next shift doesn't start by asking. It starts by knowing.
lp.surfaces.title: One ward. Four ways to work it.
lp.surfaces.line: Your practice management system runs the clinic. PlantãoVet runs the ward.
lp.surfaces.web.name: Web
lp.surfaces.web.body: The inpatient sheet: the hour × task grid for each patient, with prescriptions, progress notes, charges and discharge.
lp.surfaces.board.name: Wall board
lp.surfaces.board.body: One full-screen URL with the whole ward: who's admitted, what's next, what's late. No dedicated hardware.
lp.surfaces.app.name: Staff app
lp.surfaces.app.body: The shift's tasks in your pocket, sign-off at the kennel, and voice notes that become text. No walking back to a computer per dose.
lp.surfaces.station.name: Station mode
lp.surfaces.station.body: The hallway tablet, signed in as the clinic, where every action asks for the PIN of whoever is doing it.
lp.station.title: The tablet is shared. The accountability isn't.
lp.station.body: On the hallway device, the PIN signs the act, never the device. The sign-off sits under the name of the person who gave the dose, with their licence number alongside, when the act calls for it.
lp.station.who: Whoever typed the PIN answers for the act.
lp.trace.title: If it happened on the ward, it's on the record.
lp.trace.sub: Not as a report someone has to remember to run, as a consequence of working the day normally.
lp.trace.who.d: The name and, when the act requires it, the licence number of whoever carried it out.
lp.trace.when.d: The scheduled time and the real one, side by side, in your clinic's timezone.
lp.trace.what.d: The before and after of every change to a prescription, a dose or an outcome.
lp.trace.keep.d: The trail takes neither edits nor deletions: the protection lives in the database, not in an application rule. Corrections go in as addenda, and the history remains.
lp.start.title: Off paper without stopping the ward.
lp.start.a.d: Four fields. It's born with anchor hours and tolerance windows already set.
lp.start.b.t: Add the team and the kennels
lp.start.b.d: Each person with their role and a PIN. It takes a few minutes.
lp.start.c.d: Prescribe, and the task grid builds itself. That's where the handover starts to change.
lp.price.title: You pay per bed, not per person.
lp.price.sub: A bed is one patient admitted at a time. The whole team comes in at no cost per head: as many vets, techs and admins as the clinic needs.
lp.price.soft: Ward full? The software won't stop you treating.
lp.price.note: The plan's limit is soft on purpose. Going past the contracted number warns the administrator and is recorded, the admission happens all the same. A commercial rule must never interrupt clinical care. During the trial you get 10 beds.
lp.trial.title: During the 14 days, and after them.
lp.trial.sub: If you don't carry on with us, the clinic goes read-only. Nothing is deleted, and nothing is held hostage.
lp.trial.read: You still see everything: sheet, record, charges and audit trail.
lp.trial.discharge: You can still discharge the patients who are admitted.
lp.trial.export: You can still export the medical record as a PDF.
lp.trial.write: What stops is new writing: prescribing, signing off tasks, admitting.
lp.faq.title: Questions everyone asks
lp.faq.erp.q: Do I have to drop my practice management system?
lp.faq.erp.a: No. PlantãoVet handles the ward, prescription, scheduling, execution and handover. It doesn't do appointment booking, finance or stock, and it doesn't ask you to replace what you already use for those.
lp.faq.record.q: Does it replace my medical records?
lp.faq.record.a: The inpatient record lives here: prescriptions, executions, signed progress notes, events and outcome. It exports to PDF at any time, including after the trial.
lp.faq.mobile.q: Does it work on a phone?
lp.faq.mobile.a: It does. The web app is responsive across monitor, laptop and tablet; and there's the staff app for the shift's tasks at the kennel.
lp.faq.install.q: Do I have to install anything?
lp.faq.install.a: Not to use it in the browser. The staff app is a separate, optional app, the whole operation works without it.
lp.faq.beds.a: A bed is one patient admitted at the same time. Ten contracted beds means ten simultaneous admissions, how many pass through in a month doesn't change the price, and neither does the size of your team.
lp.faq.over.q: What if I go over my bed count?
lp.faq.over.a: The admission goes through. The system warns the administrator and records what happened, and nobody goes untreated over it. That's a design decision: a commercial rule cannot interrupt clinical care.
lp.faq.after.a: The clinic goes read-only. You still see everything, you can still discharge whoever is admitted, and you can still export the record. What stops is new writing. Nothing is deleted.
lp.faq.export.q: Can I take my records with me?
lp.faq.export.a: Yes. Each admission's record exports as a PDF, with the clinic's letterhead, and that export stays available even with the trial expired.
lp.faq.who.q: Who can change a recorded execution?
lp.faq.who.a: Nobody deletes and nobody rewrites. The clinical audit trail accepts neither edits nor deletions, and that's enforced by the database itself. A correction goes in as a new entry, and the previous one stays visible.
lp.faq.team.q: How many professionals can I add?
lp.faq.team.a: As many as the clinic has. We don't charge per user, and each person comes in with their role, vet, tech or admin, and their own PIN.
lp.final.title: Your next shift can start knowing where the last one stopped.
lp.final.sub: Create the clinic now and try it on the real routine, with your patients and your team. Fourteen days, and we don't ask for a card.
